title: A Semi-Parametric Dynamic Conditional Correlation Framework for Forecasting Systemic Risk: Evidence from CoVaR and Marginal Expected Shortfall
content: Accurate forecasting of systemic risk is crucial for financial stability and regulatory oversight. Traditional parametric models often fail to capture the complex, nonlinear dependence structures in financial markets, particularly during periods of distress. This paper proposes a semi-parametric dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) framework that integrates nonparametric estimation of marginal distributions with a parametric DCC specification to improve the forecasting of systemic risk measures—Conditional Value-at-Risk (CoVaR) and Marginal Expected Shortfall (MES). We employ a kernel-based quantile regression approach for marginal modeling and combine it with a DCC-GARCH structure for capturing time-varying conditional correlations. Empirical results using U.S. financial institutions’ equity returns during the 2007–2009 crisis and the post-crisis period demonstrate that the suggested semi-parametric DCC framework yields more accurate and robust forecasts of CoVaR and MES compared to fully parametric alternatives. Importantly, the SP-DCC is the only model that maintains correct unconditional and conditional coverage at the 1% VaR level during stress periods, while Gaussian-DCC significantly over-rejects. The model also exhibits superior performance in identifying systemically important institutions and tail interdependencies during stress episodes. Our findings underscore the importance of flexible marginal modeling in systemic risk measurement and provide policymakers with an enhanced toolkit for macroprudential surveillance.
